title: The Squinting Reader
briefing: Hana, 13, is reading on a bright beach. Her friend notices the black centres of Hana's eyes have shrunk to tiny dots. When Hana walks into the dim beach café, her friend watches them grow wide within a few seconds — and after a moment Hana can read the menu.
question: Why do the black centres of Hana's eyes keep changing size?

clues.title: Pinpoint pupils
clues.text: On the bright beach, the black centres of Hana's eyes have shrunk to tiny dots. She is squinting at her book.
clues.shows: the pupils shrinking in bright light

visual.unit: mm pupil width, shade → full sun

clues.title: Wide in the café
clues.text: Inside the dim café, the black centres grow wide within a few seconds. At first the menu looked dark; now she can read it.
clues.shows: the pupils opening wider in dim light

clues.title: The hand test
clues.text: Her friend covers one of Hana's eyes with a hand for ten seconds. When the hand moves away, that pupil is big, then shrinks within a second.
clues.shows: a pupil reacting to light in a second, without Hana deciding anything

clues.title: Readable in both places
clues.text: After a few seconds Hana can read comfortably in both places. Yet the beach is about ten times brighter than the café.
clues.shows: the eye keeping the light that gets inside fairly steady even though the outside light changed a lot

hypotheses.text: Her irises — the coloured rings around the pupils — are muscles that squeeze the pupils small in bright light and open them wide in dim light, controlling how much light gets into her eyes.
Her eyes are getting tired from reading.
hypotheses.flaw: Tired eyes don't change every time the light changes, and the pupils changed within seconds of the light — not after a long time reading.

hypotheses.text: The sun is damaging her eyes.
hypotheses.flaw: Damage would not undo itself in a few seconds indoors, and a pupil under a hand in the shade does exactly the same thing.

hypotheses.text: She is squinting on purpose to look cool.
hypotheses.flaw: Squinting is the eyelids. The pupils changed on their own — even under her friend's hand, where there was nothing to squint at.

prediction.prompt: As the light around Hana gets brighter — from a dim room to a bright beach — what happens to the width of her pupils?

second.question: The beach is about 10× brighter than the café. Does the light reaching the back of her eye also get 10× brighter?

transfer.context: Jamal walks out of a dark movie theatre into a sunny parking lot. For a few seconds everything looks blindingly bright and he squints, then it feels normal.
options: The movie tired his eyes out.
His pupils were wide open from the dark theatre; in the sun his irises squeeze them small so less light gets in.
Parking lots reflect more light than anything else.
transfer.retryHint: Think about what Hana's pupils did when she walked from bright into dim — Jamal is doing the opposite.
transfer.explanation: In the dark theatre Jamal's pupils were wide open to catch every bit of light. Stepping into the sun, far too much light poured in until his irises squeezed the pupils small — a few seconds of dazzle, then comfortable. It is Hana's café trip in reverse.

takeaway: Your pupils are adjustable windows. The iris squeezes them small in bright light and opens them wide in dim light — in seconds and without you deciding — so the light reaching the back of your eye stays in a comfortable range.
